title: Redwood Inference — Cloud Marketplace Security Packet (Draft for AWS/GCP Partner Review)
content:
Redwood Inference — Cloud Marketplace Security Packet
Draft for AWS Marketplace + Google Cloud Marketplace review

Document version
- Status: Draft (internal review)
- Prepared by: Security & Compliance
- Primary contacts: Olga Petrov (GRC), Marcus Lin (Security Eng)
- Executive sign-off (planned): Dr. Aisha Rahman (Security)

Important notes / intended use
- This packet is intended to support (a) AWS/GCP marketplace listing review and (b) enterprise buyer security questionnaires during marketplace procurement.
- This packet describes security controls for Redwood Inference’s platform and marketplace onboarding/provisioning flow.
- Some evidence artifacts (e.g., SOC 2 report) are shared under NDA only. See “Evidence & attachments” for distribution rules.
- This document is not a contractual commitment and does not replace the Redwood MSA/DPA or any executed SLA.

1) Service overview (what Redwood provides)
Redwood Inference is a developer-first platform for running and optimizing LLM inference across:
- Hosted API (Redwood-managed infrastructure)
- Dedicated capacity (customer-isolated GPU pools, Redwood-operated)
- Private deployments (VPC and on-prem options; customer-managed networking)

Cloud marketplace offerings
- AWS Marketplace and Google Cloud Marketplace listings provide procurement paths for Redwood plans/SKUs (Hosted, Dedicated, Private, plus add-ons such as premium support/SLA and observability retention where applicable).
- Marketplace purchase → entitlement → provisioning is integrated into the Redwood control plane. The buyer links the cloud marketplace identity/account to a Redwood organization to activate entitlements.

2) Data handling and privacy (high level)
Data categories processed
- Customer inputs: prompts / messages / requests submitted to Redwood endpoints
- Customer outputs: model responses returned to the customer
- Metadata: timestamps, request identifiers, model identifiers, token counts, latency, error codes
- Account/organization data: user identities, org IDs, API keys, SSO metadata (if enabled)

Data use
- Redwood processes customer content to provide the requested inference service.
- By default, Redwood does not use customer content to train foundation models.
- Any optional product features that store customer content (e.g., prompt logging for debugging/evals) are customer-controlled and documented in product settings and associated docs.

Data retention (summary)
- Request/response content retention: configurable; defaults may vary by plan and by customer setting.
- Operational logs (non-content): retained for security, reliability, and billing/usage analytics purposes for a limited period.
- Buyers requiring extended retention or specific retention controls should select the applicable retention/compliance add-on (where offered) and/or contract terms.

Data residency and regions
- Redwood supports multiple cloud regions for Hosted/Dedicated where available; customers may select region(s) based on product availability.
- For Private (VPC/on-prem), data residency is primarily controlled by where the deployment is hosted (customer-selected cloud region / customer data center).
- Note: Exact region availability is published in product docs and may change as new regions are added.

3) Shared responsibility model (marketplace context)
Hosted API (Redwood-managed)
- Redwood is responsible for the security of the service infrastructure, runtime, and operations.
- Customer is responsible for endpoint usage, API key management, user access to their Redwood org, and any integration they deploy that sends data to Redwood.

Dedicated capacity (Redwood-operated, customer-isolated)
- Redwood operates the underlying infrastructure and service.
- Customer is responsible for user access controls, data sent to Redwood, and configuration of any client-side encryption or network controls available for their use case.

Private deployment (VPC/on-prem)
- Customer controls their network boundary (VPC, routing, firewall rules) and is responsible for securing the environment as configured.
- Redwood provides software, deployment guidance, and (where contracted) operational support. Control distribution is defined in the Private deployment documentation and contract.

Marketplace procurement & entitlements
- AWS/GCP marketplace systems manage billing relationship and marketplace identities.
- Redwood’s control plane maps marketplace entitlements to Redwood organizations and applies entitlements to service access.

4) Security program overview
Governance
- Security ownership: Security & Compliance org under executive sponsor Dr. Aisha Rahman.
- Security engineering lead: Marcus Lin.
- GRC lead: Olga Petrov.

Risk management
- Formal risk register with periodic reviews.
- Security exceptions are time-bound, approved, and tracked.

Security policies
- Written policies for access control, encryption, logging/monitoring, incident response, vulnerability management, secure SDLC, and vendor/subprocessor management.

Training
- Security awareness training required for employees with periodic refreshers.

5) Identity, authentication, and access control
Customer access
- Redwood Console supports role-based access control at the organization level.
- SSO: SAML/SSO supported for eligible plans (where enabled by the customer).

Internal access
- Least privilege access model; administrative actions require authenticated access and are logged.
- MFA enforced for privileged access to production systems.
- Access is provisioned via role-based groups and is reviewed on a scheduled basis.

Vendor portal access (AWS/GCP marketplaces)
- Access to AWS/GCP partner/vendor portals is restricted to designated submitters.
- MFA is required and access is audited.
- Credentials and access are rotated/reviewed per the internal vendor-management process.

6) Encryption and key management
Encryption in transit
- Customer-to-Redwood traffic is encrypted in transit using TLS.
- Internal service-to-service communication is encrypted in transit where applicable.

Encryption at rest
- Data stored by Redwood is encrypted at rest using cloud-provider encryption mechanisms.
- Keys are managed via cloud KMS for Hosted/Dedicated environments.

Customer-managed keys (Private)
- For Private deployments (VPC/on-prem), customers may integrate with their own key management systems (KMS/HSM) depending on deployment mode and architecture.

Key management controls
- Key access is restricted and audited.
- Key rotation practices follow cloud-provider and internal security guidelines.

7) Network security and tenant isolation
Hosted API
- Production environments are segmented and protected by firewall/security group controls.
- Administrative access paths are restricted.

Dedicated capacity
- Customer isolation is enforced at the infrastructure/service layer for the dedicated pool.

Private (VPC/on-prem)
- Deployed into a customer-controlled network boundary (VPC or on-prem).
- Inbound/outbound connectivity is customer-configured within supported deployment patterns.

8) Logging, monitoring, and auditability
Security logging
- Redwood generates audit logs for security-relevant events (e.g., authentication events, privilege changes, entitlement/provisioning events).
- Marketplace onboarding events (entitlement ingestion, validation, mapping) are logged for auditability and troubleshooting.

Operational monitoring
- Monitoring covers service availability and performance, including marketplace provisioning pipeline metrics (e.g., webhook failures, entitlement lag timers).
- Alerts route to on-call/SRE per internal escalation processes.

Customer-facing observability
- Customers have access to usage and operational dashboards in the Redwood Console (subject to plan and feature availability).
- Extended observability retention may be available as an add-on (where offered).

9) Secure SDLC, vulnerability management, and change control
Secure development
- Code changes undergo peer review.
- Changes are tracked via tickets/PRs; releases follow staged rollout practices for higher-risk components.

Dependency and vulnerability management
- Vulnerabilities are tracked and remediated based on severity.
- Regular scanning is used to identify known issues.

Penetration testing
- Redwood performs periodic penetration testing with third-party support and tracks findings through remediation.

10) Incident response and business continuity
Incident response
- Written incident response process with defined severity levels and roles.
- Post-incident reviews are conducted for significant incidents.

Business continuity / disaster recovery
- Service resiliency practices include redundancy and operational monitoring.
- Recovery objectives may vary by deployment mode and contract/SLA.

11) Marketplace-specific security details (AWS/GCP)
Entitlement ingestion and validation
- Redwood validates and processes marketplace entitlement events.
- Events are handled with idempotency and retries to reduce risk of duplicate or missing provisioning.
- Provisioning events are audit logged.

Organization linking
- Buyers link a marketplace purchase to a Redwood organization.
- The console flow displays entitlement status and guides resolution for common edge cases (e.g., wrong org, region mismatch).

12) Compliance statements (current posture)
SOC 2
- Redwood maintains a SOC 2 Type II attestation.
- The SOC 2 report is available under NDA upon request.

ISO 27001
- Redwood maintains an information security program aligned with ISO 27001 control principles.
- If a formal ISO certificate is required for procurement, coordinate with Security & Compliance for the current status and available evidence.

Privacy and DPAs
- Redwood supports execution of a Data Processing Addendum (DPA) for customers requiring it (typically via direct contract; marketplace procurement may require an addendum path depending on the marketplace program).

Note: Specific compliance requirements and commitments are governed by executed agreements. This section is intended as a high-level posture summary for review.

13) Evidence & attachments (what we can share)
Distribution rules
- Public/marketplace-review shareable: documents safe to share with AWS/GCP reviewers without NDA.
- NDA-only: documents that require NDA prior to sharing with prospects/customers/partners.
- Internal only: for Redwood employees; not shared externally.

Attachment list (draft)
A) Marketplace-review shareable
1. Security overview (this packet)
2. High-level architecture & data flow diagram (Hosted/Dedicated/Private overview)
3. Encryption overview (at-rest/in-transit summary)
4. Logging & audit logging overview (including marketplace provisioning events)
5. Subprocessor list (current as of packet date) or link to published subprocessor page (if applicable)
6. Responsible disclosure / security contact instructions

B) NDA-only
1. SOC 2 Type II report (most recent) — NDA required
2. Penetration test attestation letter or executive summary — NDA required
3. Detailed infrastructure/network diagrams — NDA required

C) Internal only
1. Full risk register excerpts
2. Internal incident response runbooks
3. Vendor portal access audit records

How to request evidence
- Internal: File a request with Security & Compliance (GRC) and include: recipient, purpose, required deadline, and whether NDA is in place.
- External: Buyers should contact their Redwood account team or security@redwoodinference.com; Redwood will provide NDA instructions where needed.

14) Security contacts
- Security inquiries / evidence requests: security@redwoodinference.com
- Compliance inquiries: compliance@redwoodinference.com
- Marketplace onboarding support: marketplace-support@redwoodinference.com (or standard support channel for contracted customers)

15) Open items / TODO (before submission)
- Confirm final approved wording for data retention defaults vs configurable settings (avoid ambiguity between plan defaults and customer settings).
- Insert final diagrams/screenshots once redaction review is complete.
- Validate marketplace-specific statements for AWS vs GCP formatting requirements.
- Confirm which evidence attachments AWS/GCP reviewers will accept via partner portals vs secure email.
- Executive sign-off (Aisha Rahman) + SecEng accuracy sign-off (Marcus Lin) + GRC distribution review (Olga Petrov).

Change log (draft)
- 2025-01-12: Initial compilation from security FAQ + evidence index
- 2025-01-24: Added marketplace entitlement/audit logging section; aligned language with provisioning implementation notes
- 2025-02-03: Updated evidence distribution rules; clarified shared responsibility by deployment mode
